headline: Tissue-scale process models couple mechanics, transport and EGFR/ERK signalling
label: Multiscale Tissue Process Modelling
summary: Live-cell imaging and organ-scale simulations now allow governing tissue dynamics to be tested against measured biological readouts.
synthesis: The four published items share a process-model approach at tissue scale, implemented either as forward simulation or as inference from data. A three-dimensional Newtonian flow study tests how ciliary density, cluster spacing and metachrony govern transport and mixing. V-Cornea, an agent-based CompuCell3D model, couples corneal epithelial homeostasis and EGF signalling to injury recovery, with ocular irritation assessment as the stated aim. A mathematical model of Gurken secretion, perivitelline diffusion and EGFR activation addresses signalling distribution in Drosophila egg chambers. The distinctive advance is an inverse modelling framework that infers governing mechano-chemical equations from live-cell imaging of MAPK/ERK-driven epithelial sheet migration. The dominant thread is methodological, linking process models to concrete readouts rather than a shared mechanism across these systems.
